What you agree on the call gets signed.

Pitch deck · 2026

RockSign turns client calls into signed agreements. Opening line: "How many times have you closed a job on a video call and never put it in writing?"

The problem

Freelancers close deals by word of mouth. And words get lost.

Scope creep

“While you're at it, could you also…?” With no written scope, every extra ask looks included.

Late payments

Without signed dates and amounts, getting paid depends on the client's memory.

“I never said that”

When a dispute comes up, the only evidence is what each side remembers from the call.

Writing a contract after every call takes hours. So it gets postponed… and never happens.

Three pains every freelancer recognizes. The agreement exists: it was said on the call. What's missing is someone writing it down and getting it signed. If you have your own data (surveys, freelancer interviews), put a number here.

The solution

You talk.
RockSign writes.
Everyone signs.

RockSign listens to your client calls and, when you hang up, sends every participant a draft agreement with deliverables, dates, amounts and terms, ready to sign.

This is the core moment of the pitch. Pause after the headline. RockSign doesn't replace the conversation with the client: it turns it into a signed document with no extra work.

How it works

From call to signature, without writing a line.

01

Listen

Joins your Meet, Zoom or Teams call and tells everyone it's recording.

02

Understand

Detects deliverables, dates, amounts, revision rounds and payment terms.

03

Draft

Writes a clear draft, with every clause linked to its minute in the call.

04

Sign

When the call ends, it goes to every participant. They sign from their phone.

Optional review: the freelancer can tweak the draft before it goes out.

Four steps. Step 03 is the differentiator: every clause is tied to the exact moment in the recording where it was agreed. The recording notice in step 01 is not optional: it's what makes the agreement defensible and earns the client's trust.

This is the screen the client receives by email or WhatsApp. The timestamps are the key: if anyone doubts a clause, they hear it in their own voice. That stops disputes before they start.

Why now

Three years ago, this couldn't be built.

Voice is now text

Automatic transcription in English and Spanish is accurate and cheap.

AI understands deals

Pulling deliverables, dates and amounts out of a free-form chat is now feasible.

E-signatures are valid

Legally recognized in the US (ESIGN Act), the EU (eIDAS) and Argentina (Law 25,506).

Three curves crossed: transcription, language models and legal acceptance of e-signatures. On top of that, freelance work now closes over video calls. Before presenting, have a lawyer check the legal scope per country.

The categories are broadly right, but check each competitor's current features before presenting: notetakers add features fast. The moat isn't a single feature, it's the end-to-end flow plus the network of clients who sign.

Roadmap

From the first signed agreement to a network of trust.

PHASE 1 · [Q_ 2027]

MVP

Upload the recording or the call link and get a draft ready to sign.

PHASE 2 · [Q_ 2027]

Live

Bot for Zoom, Meet and Teams. Templates by trade: design, dev, video.

PHASE 3 · [Q_ 2028]

Follow-through

Delivery and payment reminders tied to the agreement. Invoicing integrations.

Phase 1 can be built in weeks: it needs no live bot, just processing a recording. It validates whether the generated draft is good enough for the client to sign without changes.
